closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Sixty-one supplied landing images existed in the repository and none of them was rendered by any public page, because no public landing page existed. UI-05 curated thirty-two of them into a measured manifest with responsive AVIF/WebP derivatives, and deliberately did not claim the defect: a manifest is not a rendered page.
closures.root_cause: The eight public landing pages had never been built. `/` served a foundation-only account entry card by design (Phase UI-02), so the curated imagery had no surface to appear on.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The acceptance criterion in the UI-01 register is that each account LANDING PAGE renders two to four of its own images. Nothing about the manifest, the derivatives or the helpers could satisfy it while the page did not exist — which is exactly why UI-05 left it open rather than closing it on the strength of the pipeline.
closures.correct_fix: The eight public landing pages render their own curated images through `LandingPicture`, which emits a <picture> with the AVIF and WebP candidates, the file's measured intrinsic dimensions, an aspect-ratio reservation, the manifest's loading strategy and fetch priority, the recorded focal point as object-position, and the curated alternative text. Each account renders exactly the four images its manifest assigns, in the regions the manifest assigns them to, and exactly one of them — the hero — is eager and high priority.
tests: tests/Feature/Ui06/Ui06LandingContractTest.php — renders only files from the account's own directory, with real dimensions and alt text; marks exactly one image per page eager and high priority; places every image in a region that actually renders
resources/spa/src/components/landing/LandingComponents.spec.ts — the LandingPicture describe block
resources/spa/src/pages/public/PublicPages.spec.ts — renders exactly one high-priority image on each account; renders no other account's images
tests/e2e/ui-06-public-landing-pages.spec.ts — 'renders its own curated images and no other account's', asserted against what the browser actually requested
scripts/ui06-public-host-smoke.mjs — every original and every derivative served by the built nginx image with the right MIME
closures.before: 32 curated images, 192 derivatives, rendered by no public page.
closures.after: All 32 render across the eight public landing pages — four per account, each in its manifest-assigned region, with one high-priority hero per page and no cross-account request.
closures.remaining_risk: Visual approval of the placements is UI-16's; every image still carries `release_status: pending_ui06_visual_review` in the UI-05 manifest, which UI-06 does not change because a visual baseline is not this phase's to approve.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: No account host served an FAQ. The approved FAQ documents existed under docs/support/faq/, and after UI-05 they compiled to 1,264 typed items, but no route rendered them and the fixed footer deliberately shipped no FAQ link rather than a dead one.
closures.root_cause: There was no public FAQ route. UI-05 supplied the compiled data and the SvFaq adapter and explicitly added no route.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The acceptance criterion is a reachable public FAQ route per account. Compiled data with no route is unreachable by definition.
closures.correct_fix: `/faq` on every approved account host, serving that account's own compiled FAQ in full. The account is host-derived — no path segment, query parameter or stored value can select a different one. Rendering goes through UI-04's SvFaq (native <details>/<summary>, keyboard-operable without ARIA of its own); the source's own category dividers are preserved as headings so a 196-question document stays navigable. The fixed footer now links it, because the destination finally exists.
tests: tests/Feature/Ui06/Ui06LandingContractTest.php — publishes an FAQ route on every account host, serving that account's own questions; carries the full compiled FAQ including the sixty questions UI05-FAQ-001 recovered
resources/spa/src/pages/public/PublicPages.spec.ts — eight accounts, each rendering exactly its own compiled item count, with unique disclosure ids
tests/e2e/ui-06-public-landing-pages.spec.ts — 'serves its own FAQ at /faq' for all eight, including keyboard operation
scripts/ui06-public-host-smoke.mjs — /faq answered by the built edge on all eight account hosts
closures.before: 0 of 8 hosts served an FAQ; 1,264 compiled items were unreachable.
closures.after: 8 of 8 hosts serve /faq; every compiled item is on the page, none hidden behind a filter or a page size.
closures.remaining_risk: The largest FAQ is 196 items on one page. No client-side search was added: the source is grouped by its own category dividers and the plan does not require search, so adding one would have been an unrequested feature rather than a proven need. If usability review finds otherwise, it is a small addition on top of this route.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: No account host served a public landing page, and the legal documents were reachable only through a role-parameterised path (/legal/:role/:doc) in which the account came from the URL rather than from the host.
closures.root_cause: Two distinct gaps behind one defect id: the landing pages did not exist, and the legal route selected its account from a path segment.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: A public legal document is only correct if the account that owns it is decided by something the visitor cannot change. A role in the path is exactly that kind of input, whatever the page then does with it.
closures.correct_fix: Twenty-four canonical routes — /legal/data-policy, /legal/privacy-policy and /legal/terms-of-service on each of the eight account hosts — with the account resolved from the server-provided host context and the document slug matched by a closed alternation in the route itself. Every internal link was migrated: the fixed footer and the authenticated role landing now build destinations through `publicLegalLocation()`. The old shape survives as a compatibility route only: the account's own documents redirect to the canonical path, and any other role fails closed without rendering and without redirecting to another host.
tests: tests/Feature/Ui06/Ui06LandingContractTest.php — publishes twenty-four canonical legal routes, three per account; serves each account its own documents verbatim from its own source; builds no legal destination that carries a role in the path
resources/spa/src/pages/public/PublicPages.spec.ts — 24 mounts, each asserting the account key, the source path and the source hash, and the absence of every other account
resources/spa/src/layouts/RoleLayouts.spec.ts — the footer links the canonical paths and no account key survives in a destination
tests/e2e/ui-06-public-landing-pages.spec.ts — 'serves its own three legal documents at role-free paths', plus the legacy-path redirect and the mismatched-role denial
scripts/ui06-public-host-smoke.mjs — the three legal paths answered by the built edge on all eight hosts
closures.before: 0 of 8 hosts served a landing page; the legal account came from the path.
closures.after: 8 landing pages and 24 canonical legal routes; the legal account comes from the server-resolved host and cannot be selected by a visitor.
closures.remaining_risk: The compatibility route still exists. It is covered by tests in both directions, and removing it belongs to whichever phase can prove no external link depends on it.

closures.observed_problem: Four accounts supply a testimonials section carrying customer evidence that cannot be published. merchant_branch, merchant_finance and merchant_front_office each present an attributed customer quotation with no verified source; merchant_personnel states in the source itself that its three quotations are suggestions to be replaced before launch.
closures.resolution: Binding product-owner decision §2.1: no supplied customer testimonial quotation is approved for production, and all eight public landing pages use an approved factual trust-evidence alternative instead. No source text was deleted or rewritten; the sections remain compiled, hashed and flagged `renderPermitted: false`, and the page's single publication gate is that flag.
closures.implementation: A typed `TrustEvidenceItem` whose vocabulary contains no category capable of carrying a customer claim, and whose `customerClaim` and `metricClaim` fields are typed as the literal `false` — an unverified quotation cannot be expressed in the type at all. Each item names the repository source that backs it. The region renders no blockquote, no quotation mark, no attribution and no logo.
tests: tests/Feature/Ui06/Ui06LandingContractTest.php — publishes no customer evidence on any account; backs every item with a real repository source; renders no quotation styling; contains no fabricated customer evidence anywhere in the public landing source
resources/spa/src/content/landing/landingComposition.spec.ts — the trust-evidence describe block, including the forbidden-pattern scan
resources/spa/src/components/landing/LandingComponents.spec.ts — renders no blockquote, cite or quotation mark
tests/e2e/ui-06-public-landing-pages.spec.ts — per-account assertions that every rendered item declares customer_claim=false and metric_claim=false
closures.before: Four accounts carried an unpublishable testimonials section; three carried none.
closures.after: Eight accounts carry a distinct, source-backed factual trust-evidence region. No quotation, rating, adoption figure or performance claim is reachable in the built pages.
closures.remaining_risk: If verified customer evidence is supplied later, the region has a defined second state (§8.4 state 1) and would need its own review. Nothing about the current implementation makes that harder.

closures.observed_problem: Four of the sixteen plan regions had no source content: merchant_administrator, merchant_audit and super_administrator supply no testimonials section, and super_administrator supplies no pricing section.
closures.resolution: Binding product-owner decisions §2.2 and §2.3. The three missing testimonials regions carry the same approved factual trust-evidence alternative as the other five. The missing Super Administrator pricing region carries approved plan-access-and-administration content: the account administers platform plan availability, merchant subscriptions are not purchased from this page, no merchant subscription price is offered to it, and no amount is shown.

additional_finding.finding: The Merchant Administrator pricing section is the only one of the eight that states amounts — four tiers between KES 2,000 and KES 12,000 per month.
additional_finding.evidence: The canonical price authority is the plan-price catalogue the platform operator maintains at runtime (`subscription_plan_prices`, Phase 20A). No seeder or config file supplies it, and no public endpoint exposes it: GET /api/v1/subscription/plans requires an authenticated merchant session and the platform catalogue requires `platform.plan.view`.
additional_finding.consequence: A public page cannot prove any amount is current, and UI/UX plan §8.5 forbids showing a stale one. Binding decision §2.4 applies: the role-appropriate plan-access explanation and no amount. The four tier blocks are withheld with the reason recorded in pricing-plan-access-matrix.json; the source is unchanged and remains compiled and hashed.

closures.implementation: `PlanAccessBlock.showsAmount` and `purchaseCta` are typed as the literal `false`, and the component has no branch capable of rendering a price or a purchase action. Content the page withholds is stated to the visitor rather than silently omitted.

resources/spa/src/content/landing/landingComposition.spec.ts — the plan-access describe block

closures.before: Three testimonials regions and one pricing region had no source; one pricing region stated unprovable amounts.
closures.after: All sixteen regions are present on all eight pages. No page states an amount, and every withholding carries a recorded reason.
closures.remaining_risk: The Merchant Administrator page no longer shows plan prices, which is a deliberate reduction in published information. If the product owner wants amounts on the public page, the durable fix is a public, cache-controlled plan-price endpoint reading the live catalogue — a backend change outside UI-06's declared scope (§29) that must be authorized on its own.

decisions_recorded.observed: The approved landing sources for all six invitation-based accounts, and for Super Administrator, declare a GET STARTED action that opens 'login and create account'. The account-host registry marks all seven `selfRegistration: false`.
decisions_recorded.authority: Binding decision §2.5 — only the Merchant Administrator account may expose merchant self-registration; no invitation-based account may expose open self-registration; Super Administrator may not expose merchant registration. Where a source CTA contradicts the current registry, the security boundary wins and the conflict is recorded.
decisions_recorded.resolution: Those seven pages offer sign-in as the primary action. The six invitation accounts additionally offer invitation acceptance at the existing host-relative /staff/accept route. The registration route is not linked from any of them, which the browser proof asserts per account.
decisions_recorded.owner: recorded — no further action required in UI-06

decisions_recorded.observed: Prose in some invitation-account sources still refers to the GET STARTED action by name — Human Resource's first step reads 'Use GET STARTED to create a business account or log in', and Branch's FAQ asks 'What happens when I click GET STARTED?'. Those pages no longer show a button with that label.
decisions_recorded.why_not_fixed_here: The text is approved product-owner copy describing the product's onboarding model, and rewriting it is forbidden (CLAUDE.md §9). It links nowhere and exposes no action; it is a wording mismatch, not an exposed capability.
decisions_recorded.entry_condition: The source copy is revised, or the product owner records that the wording is acceptable.
decisions_recorded.risk_if_ignored: A visitor on an invitation host reads about an action the page does not offer.

decisions_recorded.observed: Every source writes its primary call to action as **GET STARTED**, in capitals.
decisions_recorded.authority: docs/brand/Servana Brand Identity.md, 'Buttons': "Use sentence case. Good: Create invoice. Avoid: CREATE INVOICE."
decisions_recorded.resolution: Labels are rendered in sentence case ('Get started', 'Log in'). The action and the destination are unchanged; only the casing follows the brand authority. Asserted for every CTA on every account.
decisions_recorded.owner: recorded — no further action required in UI-06

decisions_recorded.observed: The pre-UI-06 route /legal/:role/:doc selected the account from a path segment. The plan requires the canonical public route to be host-derived and role-free.
decisions_recorded.resolution: Internal links were migrated to the canonical paths. The old shape is retained as a compatibility route: with a resolved account context, a role equal to the host account redirects to the canonical path and any other role fails closed without rendering and without redirecting to another host. With NO resolved context — the standalone Vite preview origin embeds none — there is no host account for the rule to compare against, so behaviour is unchanged from before this phase. In production the shell always embeds a context, so the restriction always applies.
decisions_recorded.owner: recorded — removal belongs to whichever phase can prove no external link depends on it

decisions_recorded.observed: Finance and Human Resource declare the same four in-page navigation links (Features, How It Works, Security, FAQ) because their approved source header sections declare the same four.
decisions_recorded.resolution: Not forced apart: inventing navigation neither document asks for would be exactly the fabrication §15.1 forbids. The distinctness contract asserts the unique COMBINATION of every distinguishing axis (§14.2) and additionally guards that no THIRD account joins the shared pair.
decisions_recorded.owner: recorded — no further action required in UI-06

decisions_recorded.entry_condition: A public, cache-controlled plan-price endpoint reading the live catalogue is authorized, or the product owner accepts that the public page states no amount.
decisions_recorded.risk_if_ignored: None to correctness. The public page publishes less commercial information than the source document contains.
